desc:
Given an integer array nums (values may be negative) and a positive integer k, find the maximum sum over all contiguous subarrays whose length is a multiple of k (k, 2k, 3k, ...).

Since nums.length ≥ k, at least one such subarray always exists.

nums = [1, 2, -3, 4], k = 2
length 2: 3, -1, 1;   length 4: 4
result = 4
hints: Trying all start and end positions is O(n<sup>2</sup>). Express a subarray sum as a difference of two prefix sums.
A subarray from prefix index i to j has length j - i, which is a multiple of k exactly when i % k == j % k.

For each residue class of the prefix index keep the minimum prefix sum seen so far. For every j, the best subarray ending there is P[j] - minPrefix[j % k] (only when that class already has an earlier entry).
editorial: With prefix sums P[0..n], the subarray covering positions i..j-1 has sum P[j] - P[i] and length j - i. The length is a positive multiple of k iff i < j and i ≡ j (mod k).

So the prefix indices split into k classes by index modulo k, and within a class we want the largest difference P[j] - P[i] with i < j. Scan j from 0 to n, maintain the minimum prefix sum of each class, and update the answer with P[j] - min[class] before updating that minimum. This is O(n) time and O(k) space. It is the 'best time to buy and sell' idea applied separately to each index residue.
